title: Tail Runs Out of Memory
symptom: tail() returns the right lines, but on a 20 GB log the process is killed for memory. It only needs 10 lines.
failingTest:
import unittest
from tail import tail
from fakefile import FakeFile


class Failing(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_does_not_slurp(self):
        f = FakeFile(["a\n", "b\n", "c\n", "d\n", "e\n"])
        self.assertEqual(tail(f, 3), ["c\n", "d\n", "e\n"])
rootCause: readlines() materializes every line before slicing, so memory is O(file size). A bounded buffer of n lines (deque with maxlen) gives O(n) memory in one pass.

wrongFixes.whyWrong: Trimming in batches looks bounded, but buf[-0:] is the whole list, so n == 0 never trims and returns every line.

grading.question: What is the memory complexity before and after?
Why is buf[-n:] dangerous when n can be 0?
grading.ideal: -0 is 0, so the slice is the entire list.

turns.text: tail() runs out of memory on a 20 GB log. It only needs the last few lines.
readlines() loads the whole file before slicing. A deque with maxlen=n keeps only the last n lines while reading the file once, so memory stays proportional to n.

test_failing: OK (1 test)
test_regression: OK (4 tests)
Both suites pass, including n = 0 and a file shorter than n.

transcript.verdict: Approve. One pass, memory bounded by n, and the edge cases a hand-rolled buffer usually gets wrong (n = 0, fewer lines than n) are covered by deque itself and by the tests it ran.
